title: Functorial simplicial localization and filtered-colimit compatibility
statement: Use small simplicial sets, collections of edges, quasicategories, coherent functor categories and equivalence edges of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], and localization as in [def-coef-universally-localizing-simplicial-map]. There is a choice, for every small simplicial set $C$ and collection $W\subseteq C_1$, of a quasicategory $L(C,W)$ and a simplicial map $F_{C,W}:C\to L(C,W)$ exhibiting $L(C,W)$ as a localization of $C$ at $W$. This choice is strictly functorial on pairs: a simplicial map $a:C\to C'$ with $a(W)\subseteq W'$ induces $L(a):L(C,W)\to L(C',W')$, with $L(a)F_{C,W}=F_{C',W'}a$, $L(1)=1$ and $L(ba)=L(b)L(a)$. It preserves filtered colimits in the following sense. Let $I$ be a small nonempty ordinary category in which every finite diagram has a cocone, and let $(C_i,W_i)$ be a strict diagram of such pairs. Set $C=\operatorname{colim}_i C_i$ degreewise and $W=\bigcup_i\operatorname{image}(W_i\to C_1)$. Then the canonical map $\operatorname{colim}_i L(C_i,W_i)\to L(C,W)$ is an isomorphism of simplicial sets, carrying the colimit of the maps $F_{C_i,W_i}$ to $F_{C,W}$.

source.place: Kerodon Proposition 6.3.2.11 (05ZP): existence of C[W^{-1}], functoriality, and commutation with filtered colimits. Kerodon tag, not a Stacks tag; read online 2026-10-17; archived source WANTED.

proof.text: Fix the finite simplicial set $Q$ and its map $e:\Delta^1\to Q$ from [lem-coef-simplicial-edge-inversion-pushout]. For each pair $(C,W)$ form its explicit degreewise pushout $D(C,W)=C\amalg_{\coprod_W\Delta^1}\coprod_WQ$, with structure map $j_{C,W}:C\to D(C,W)$. The cited statement says exactly that $j_{C,W}^*$ is a coherent functor equivalence onto the full category of $W$-inverting diagrams, for every quasicategory target, even though $D(C,W)$ need not yet be a quasicategory.

source.place: Corollary 6.3.2.9; online source read, archive WANTED

proof.text: For a map of pairs $a:(C,W)\to(C',W')$, send the summand indexed by $w$ to that indexed by $a(w)$ by the identity of $\Delta^1$ or $Q$, and use $a$ on $C$. The representing-edge maps commute with these assignments. The pushout property therefore defines $D(a)$ with $D(a)j_{C,W}=j_{C',W'}a$. On all coproduct summands and on $C$, the maps for an identity and a composite agree with the corresponding identity and composite. Uniqueness in the degreewise pushout gives $D(1)=1$ and $D(ba)=D(b)D(a)$.

source.place: Proposition 6.3.2.11, functoriality of the pushout construction; online source read, archive WANTED

proof.text: Apply [lem-coef-filtered-inner-horn-factorization] to $f:D(C,W)\to\Delta^0$. Put $R(X)=T(X\to\Delta^0)$ and $r_X=u_{X\to\Delta^0}$. The map $R(X)\to\Delta^0$ is an inner fibration, so its lifting property says precisely that $R(X)$ is a quasicategory. Naturality of $T$ gives $R(a)r_X=r_Ya$ and the exact functor laws. Define $L(C,W)=R(D(C,W))$ and $F_{C,W}=r_{D(C,W)}j_{C,W}$. The two functor laws and the two naturality equations now give all three strict functoriality equations required for $L$ and $F$.

source.place: Proposition 4.1.3.2 applied over the terminal simplicial set; online source read, archive WANTED

proof.text: Each $r_X$ is inner anodyne. By [lem-coef-joyal-model-structure], every inner horn inclusion is a Joyal trivial cofibration. Thus every Joyal fibration is an inner fibration. The left lifting property defining $r_X$ gives its left lifting property against every Joyal fibration; the weak factorization system in that node identifies it as a Joyal trivial cofibration. By [lem-coef-joyal-functor-equivalence-test], for every quasicategory $E$ the actual restriction $r_X^*:\operatorname{Fun}(R(X),E)\to\operatorname{Fun}(X,E)$ is a coherent functor equivalence.

source.place: Proposition 6.3.2.11: inner-anodyne replacement does not change the localization; online source read, archive WANTED

proof.text: For every quasicategory $E$, restriction along $F_{C,W}$ is the composite $j_{C,W}^*r_{D(C,W)}^*$. The second factor is a coherent equivalence by the preceding step and [lem-coef-joyal-functor-equivalence-test]; the first factors as a coherent equivalence onto the full subcategory of $W$-inverting diagrams by [lem-coef-simplicial-edge-inversion-pushout]. Compose their quasi-inverses and their coherent inverse equivalences. This is exactly the localization property in [def-coef-universally-localizing-simplicial-map], with quasicategory target $L(C,W)$ already established.

source.place: Proposition 6.3.2.11: composite localization; online source read, archive WANTED

proof.text: For the filtered diagram in the statement, the map $\operatorname{colim}_i W_i\to W$ is surjective by the definition of $W$. If $w_i,w_j$ have the same image in $C_1$, the description of a set colimit as a quotient gives a finite zigzag of transition relations identifying them. A cocone on that finite zigzag provides one stage at which their edge images agree. Their images still belong to that stage's marking, so they are equal there as elements of the subset $W_k\subseteq(C_k)_1$. This proves injectivity. The same argument shows that any compatible family of functions $W_i\to S$ gives a unique function $W\to S$. No transition map is assumed injective.

source.place: Proposition 6.3.2.11: filtered colimit of the markings; online source read, archive WANTED

proof.text: In degree $n$, a map $D(C,W)_n\to S$ is exactly a function $C_n\to S$ and a family of functions $Q_n\to S$ indexed by $W$, agreeing on the corresponding copies of $(\Delta^1)_n$. By the colimit property of $C_n$ and the preceding identification $\operatorname{colim}W_i=W$, these data are exactly compatible families of such data for $(C_i,W_i)$. Consequently the canonical map $\operatorname{colim}_iD(C_i,W_i)\to D(C,W)$ is bijective in each degree. Its compatibility with operators and with the maps from $C_i$ follows by restriction on the same summands. It is therefore an isomorphism of simplicial sets carrying $\operatorname{colim}j_{C_i,W_i}$ to $j_{C,W}$.

source.place: Proposition 6.3.2.11: the explicit pushout commutes with filtered colimits; online source read, archive WANTED

proof.text: The constant diagram at $\Delta^0$ has colimit $\Delta^0$: the index category is nonempty and any two objects have a common recipient, so its set of components is a singleton. Therefore the colimit of the arrows $D(C_i,W_i)\to\Delta^0$ is $D(C,W)\to\Delta^0$, under the preceding degreewise isomorphism. Apply the filtered-colimit and structural-map clauses of [lem-coef-filtered-inner-horn-factorization]. They give the canonical isomorphism $\operatorname{colim}_i R(D(C_i,W_i))\to R(D(C,W))$, and identify the colimit of the $r_{D(C_i,W_i)}$ with $r_{D(C,W)}$. Composing with the identified colimit of the $j_{C_i,W_i}$ gives precisely $F_{C,W}$. This is the required comparison map and its asserted compatibility with $F$.

source.place: Proposition 6.3.2.11: compose the two filtered-colimit-preserving constructions; online source read, archive WANTED

split_report.summary: Kept the statement. Expanded the Kerodon construction into its finite inverse-gadget pushout and a general filtered-colimit-preserving inner-horn factorization. Proved strict functoriality and both colimit comparisons from their explicit universal properties, including noninjective transitions and the marking colimit. Used existing Joyal lifting and functor-equivalence statements for replacement invariance. Two new statement-only nodes; no Mathlib match.

I checked Kerodon online: 05ZP (proof: combine 6.3.2.9 with 4.1.3.2), 05ZL (any simplicial set C and any W; D need not be an infinity-category), 05ZJ (Q = Delta^3 with edges 02 and 13 collapsed to separate points), 05ZK (e = edge 12) and 01BP (factorization of any arrow, functorial and commuting with filtered colimits). The item's statement is unchanged, a faithful precise form of 05ZP. Edge-inversion node: matches 05ZL exactly; tested on W empty, C=Delta^1 with W={01}, and a degenerate edge. Factorization node: matches 01BP and is true by the small-object argument with finite generators. Steps: 1-3 build L = R(D) with strict functoriality, and the summand map w to a(w) handles merged markings. Step 4: inner horns are Joyal trivial cofibrations and the weak factorization system makes r a trivial cofibration, so joyal-functor-equivalence-test (i)=>(ii) applies. Step 5 composes the two equivalences, as the definition requires. Step 6 holds because filtered colimits of sets preserve injections and W_k is a subset of (C_k)_1. Steps 7-8 are the degreewise pushout and the colimit clause, using connectedness for colim Delta^0. Duplicate search with rg (05ZL/05ZJ/05ZK/05ZP/01BP, inner anodyne, filtered-colimit factorization) found no existing statement; the closest candidates (relative-marked-anodyne-replacement, coherent-inner-anodyne-equivalences, universal-localization-pushout, joyal-model-structure) are different. Proof route stays in unit sk-prop-sf-biduality-general, with no cycle, no SGA and no tool_uses. No fixes.

lean.statement: theorem exists_simplicial_localization : ∃ choice : SimplicialLocalizationChoice.{u, v}, ∀ (I : Type u) [SmallCategory I] [IsFiltered I] (D : I ⥤ SSet.{u}) (W : ∀ i, Set ((D.obj i) _⦋1⦌)) (hW : ∀ {i j : I} (f : i ⟶ j) (w : (D.obj i) _⦋1⦌), w ∈ W i → (D.map f).app _ w ∈ W j), ∃ (K : I ⥤ SSet.{u}) (e : ∀ i, K.obj i ≅ choice.L (D.obj i) (W i)), (∀ {i j : I} (f : i ⟶ j), K.map f ≫ (e j).hom = (e i).hom ≫ choice.map (D.map f) (hW f)) ∧ ∃ (q : colimit D ⟶ colimit K) (r : colimit K ⟶ choice.L (colimit D) (⋃ i, (colimit.ι D i).app (op ⦋1⦌) '' W i)), IsIso r ∧ (∀ i, colimit.ι D i ≫ q = choice.F (D.obj i) (W i) ≫ (e i).inv ≫ colimit.ι K i) ∧ (∀ i, colimit.ι K i ≫ r = (e i).hom ≫ choice.map (colimit.ι D i) (by intro w hw exact Set.mem_iUnion.mpr ⟨i, Set.mem_image_of_mem _ hw⟩)) ∧ q ≫ r = choice.F (colimit D) (⋃ i, (colimit.ι D i).app (op ⦋1⦌) '' W i)
lean.note: SimplicialLocalizationChoice packages precisely the choice, localization property and strict map laws of this node. The theorem additionally supplies a localized diagram identified objectwise and on every transition map, its canonical filtered-colimit comparison isomorphism, and compatibility with the universal maps. No object is chosen from the existence theorem.
